module_title: Peasant Movements in the 20th Century - Integration with Nationalism and Communism
introduction: This advanced level analyzes how 20th-century peasant movements evolved. They no longer remained localized but merged with the broader Indian National Movement (under Gandhi) and later came under the strong influence of Leftist (Communist) ideologies.

core_concepts.title: Champaran (1917) and Kheda (1918)
core_concepts.description: These marked the entry of Gandhi into peasant struggles. Champaran was against the 'Tinkathia' system (forcing farmers to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land). Kheda was a no-tax campaign due to crop failure.

core_concepts.title: Moplah (Malabar) Rebellion (1921)
core_concepts.description: Muslim peasants (Moplahs) in Kerala rebelled against Hindu landlords (Jenmis) and the British. Initially supported by Khilafat leaders, it later took a tragic communal turn.

core_concepts.title: All India Kisan Sabha (1936)
core_concepts.description: Formed in Lucknow to bring peasant movements under a single national umbrella. It demanded the abolition of Zamindari, reduction of land revenue, and institutionalization of credit.

core_concepts.title: Tebhaga Movement (1946)
core_concepts.description: A massive communist-led movement in Bengal. The sharecroppers (Bargadars) demanded that they should keep two-thirds (Tebhaga) of the crop produce, and give only one-third to the landlords (Jotedars), as recommended by the Floud Commission.

core_concepts.title: Telangana Armed Struggle (1946-51)
core_concepts.description: A communist-led peasant rebellion against the oppressive landlords (Deshmukhs) and the Nizam of Hyderabad. It was one of the largest guerrilla peasant wars in modern Indian history.

important_entities.name: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
important_entities.significance: A militant ascetic who founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha and became the primary architect of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) in 1936.

important_entities.name: N.G. Ranga
important_entities.significance: Served as the General Secretary of the AIKS and was instrumental in organizing the peasantry in the Andhra region.

important_entities.name: Ali Musaliyar
important_entities.significance: A religious scholar who became the focal point of the anti-British and anti-landlord uprising in Malabar in 1921.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: What started as an anti-colonial and anti-landlord agrarian struggle quickly devolved into communal riots. UPSC often asks to critically analyze this shift from an agrarian to a communal uprising.
Students often confuse the fractions. The demand was NOT to give 2/3rds to the landlord, but for the sharecropper to KEEP 2/3rds and give 1/3rd to the landlord.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: T-T (Tebhaga in East, Telangana in South)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Both the Tebhaga and Telangana movements started in 1946, heavily backed by the Communist Party of India.

exam_strategy_tips: For chronologies, remember: Champaran (1917) -> Kheda (1918) -> Moplah (1921) -> Bardoli (1928) -> AIKS formation (1936).
Identify the specific commissions associated with movements, such as the Floud Commission associated with the Tebhaga Movement.
